title: Are all odd zeta values ζ(2k+1) transcendental

problemStatement.plain: Are all odd zeta values ζ(2k+1) transcendental? Not a single one is known to be transcendental. ζ(3) is irrational (Apéry 1978). Infinitely many are irrational (Rivoal 2000).

knowledge.progressSummary: SURVEY + FORMALIZATION: Created BaselProblemOQ02.lean (109 lines). Formalized the transcendence conjecture, Apéry theorem axiom, structural relationships. 2 axioms (pi_transcendental, apery_theorem), 0 sorries.
builtItems: Proved zetaValue_two and zetaValue_four from Mathlib
insights: Stark even/odd divide: ζ(2k) = rational × π^(2k) (fully understood since Euler 1734), but ζ(2k+1) has no closed form
Transcendental implies irrational via Transcendental.irrational in Mathlib
Mathlib has hasSum_zeta_two/four and hasSum_zeta_nat for even values, nothing for odd
Neither π transcendental nor Apéry theorem are in Mathlib v4.26.0
Problem inherently open - no specific odd zeta value known transcendental

Could add Zudilin result (one of ζ(5,7,9,11) irrational) as axiom
If Lindemann-Weierstrass lands in Mathlib, pi_transcendental becomes provable
